title: Clo Vendor Leaderboard: Investment And Resources
description:
We’re officially debuting the CLO Vendor Leaderboard, a platform created to connect brands with the most innovative 3D-ready partners in the industry. This year, we’re spotlighting pioneers across Hong Kong and Southeast Asia: Busana Apparel Group, Cobalt Fashion, Crystal International, GMS+, Hop Lun, Newtimes Group, Daehan Global, PT. Kahatex, and Trax Intertrade.

In the second CLO Vendor Leaderboard 5 criterias video series, 

Why do some vendors scale effortlessly while others struggle to keep up with digital demands? In the second CLO Vendor Leaderboard 5 criterias video series, Investments and Resources, we cover how these trailblazers took a proactive approach—investing heavily in hardware, asset libraries, and team upskilling. Watch as they break down how they prioritize complex 3D projects, handle rapid scaling requests from global brands, and maximize their ROI using CLO and CLO-SET features to build a strong workflow.

This series covers the 5 essentials of 3D success:
1️⃣ 3D Capacity 
2️⃣ Investment & Resources
3️⃣ Business Impact
4️⃣ Partnership
5️⃣ Strategic Vision

markdown_content: ## Investment in Speed, Scalability, and 3D Workflow Enhancements This section details the significant investments made in hardware, software, and team training to improve speed, scalability, and efficiency in 3D fashion design workflows using CLO. We invested heavily in high-end workstations equipped with powerful GPUs, enabling rendering processes to complete within minutes. Our infrastructure runs on cloud servers paired with a shared digital library containing brands, fabrics, trims, avatars, and templates. All data is backed up securely in Core Set, ensuring data integrity and accessibility. Key investments include hardware upgrades, continuous team training, and building a comprehensive library of reusable blocks and templates that accelerate development cycles. These improvements have optimized our 3D workflow, enhancing efficiency and ease of use. We prioritize understanding each project's specific needs—including design compactness, sustainability goals, and customer collaboration—to allocate resources most effectively and achieve optimal results. ## Early Adoption and Expansion of CLO Technology Across Teams This section explains the strategic adoption and expansion of CLO software licenses, skill development, and cross-department integration to meet industry demands. As early adopters of CLO, we secured multiple cloud licenses to build capacity in a technology critical for the fashion industry. Our most significant investment has been in human capital: training most of our team from scratch within Busana, expanding CLO use across design, product development, and garment technology teams. Investments span software licenses, hardware upgrades, hiring, and specialized training of 3D technicians to fulfill increasing customer demands. This comprehensive approach ensures skilled execution of 3D designs and facilitates broader organizational adoption. ## Use of CLO Fabric Kit for Accurate Fabric Digitization This section covers the technical application of CLO Fabric Kit to digitize fabrics accurately and its impact on sample fidelity and process efficiency. We utilize CLO Fabric Kit as an investment tool to digitize fabrics precisely, allowing 3D samples to replicate physical samples accurately based on 2D patterns. This capability reduces discrepancies between digital and physical samples. To maximize efficiency, specific business units focus on fabric digitization using CLO Fabric Kit, enabling the 3D team to concentrate on utilizing these digital assets in sampling workflows. ## Internal Training and Resource Allocation for Efficient 3D Operations This section outlines the internal training systems and strategic resource allocation designed to maximize team efficiency, reduce miscommunication, and improve project outcomes. We have developed a comprehensive internal training system that includes regular skill development workshops aimed at enhancing 3D expertise and encouraging broader understanding across the company. Strategically, we assign dedicated teams to fabric digitization and 3D modeling to streamline workflows. Collaboration with physical sample teams ensures continuous review and alignment between digital and physical outputs, minimizing differences and enhancing accuracy in complex or large-scale projects. ## Digital Asset Library and CLO Fabric Kit for Consistency and Realism This section describes the creation of a centralized digital asset library and the use of CLO Fabric Kit to maintain consistency and realism in 3D fashion design outputs. A significant initiative has been developing a comprehensive digital asset library containing clean cloth data, including fabrics, trims, stitch settings, and reusable templates. This library reduces setup time and improves consistency across all 3D outputs. The CLO Fabric Kit supports building a wide range of accurate digital fabrics, enabling simulations that closely mimic real-world fabric behavior. This enhances reliable decision-making during design development. ## Prioritization Criteria for Tools and Training in Complex Projects This section explains the evaluation criteria used to prioritize tool development and training investments for larger, more complex projects. When prioritizing tools or training, we assess three key factors: 1. Complexity of the style 2. Potential time savings for the team 3. Degree to which the investment improves accuracy Our goal is to bring the product closer to its real form quickly, reduce the number of physical samples needed, and increase confidence in design decisions, shaping our 3D workflow roadmap accordingly. ## Case Study: Accelerated Development with Picken Kloppenburg This section presents a case study demonstrating the speed and efficiency gains achieved through 3D digital fashion design. A German client, Picken Kloppenburg, typically required 45 to 90 days for development. Using 3D digital fashion design, their collection was developed on-site within two days. Our 3D designers created digital samples rapidly, allowing immediate feedback and adjustments. Physical orders were placed immediately, and products reached shops within three months. This process shortened the typical development timeline from six to nine months down to three months, enabling faster market responsiveness and cost savings. ## Team Training and Resource Allocation for Smooth 3D Transitions This section covers the importance of specialized training and resource allocation to support smooth client transitions to CLO workflows. We proactively allocate a dedicated 3D team trained extensively in CLO software and client-specific workflows to ensure seamless transitions without constraints. This training, often conducted in partnership with clients, equips our team with the skills needed to meet client demands efficiently, maintain project schedules, and build trust throughout the transition period. ## Size Grading and Resource Allocation for Complex Projects This section highlights the return on investment from size grading and strategic team allocation in managing complex projects. Size grading has yielded significant efficiency and cost benefits by enabling fast and accurate fit adjustments across sizes. For complex projects, success depends on allocating the right team members, leveraging their strengths, and prioritizing speed, consistency, reusable assets, and peer support. This approach minimizes approval cycles and keeps projects progressing smoothly. ## Use of 3D Visuals for Client Communication and Issue Resolution This section explains how 3D visuals aid communication with brands unfamiliar with 3D, reducing sample production and accelerating approvals. For clients new to 3D, we use clear 3D visuals to demonstrate design interpretations and propose solutions. This reduces the need for multiple physical samples, saving time, cost, and effort, while still delivering the brand’s requirements accurately. ## Scaling 3D Capabilities for Growing Client Demands This section discusses strategies for scaling 3D design resources and capabilities to meet expanding client requirements. As more clients and retailers adopt 3D design development, we expand internal 3D capabilities by hiring more trained designers and upgrading hardware. We simulate and adjust designs before physical sampling using 3D samples that visualize patterns, stitches, and garment fit, combined with virtual knitting for fully fashioned seams. This accelerates development cycles and adapts designs to client needs efficiently. ## Successful Scaling of a Partner Brand’s Seasonal Range in 3D This section describes a successful project where a partner brand expanded a 3D pilot into a full-range seasonal collection. A partner brand grew their 3D pilot from 5 styles to 28 within the same deadline. To scale, we reorganized resources by building shared 3D templates with size blocks, preset switching, and fabric physics. One team member focused exclusively on fabric digitization, while complex styles were handled by experienced staff. Reusing templates rather than starting from scratch enabled delivery three days ahead of schedule with consistent quality. Following this success, the brand committed to shifting more development into 3D. ## Future Outlook: CLO as a Game-Changer in Early Design Development This section explores the future role of CLO in accelerating design concept development, enhancing communication, and supporting customization. CLO accelerates early design stages by quickly generating concepts for customer selection, aiding in capturing market opportunities, especially with repeat styles and multiple color or laser options. The CLO Symmetry function streamlines repetitive technical tasks, improving efficiency. Colorway review features allow rapid visualization of color options without creating physical samples, speeding decision-making. Size set review validates fit and proportions across sizes early, reducing physical samples and increasing production accuracy. Fabric creation enables custom digital fabric development based on content type, maintaining drape quality and suitability across projects, thereby enhancing product quality overall.
